job.title: Senior Software Engineer, Forecasting & Real-Time Optimization
job.pay_full: $136,160 – $170,200 a year base pay (Seattle area), not including potential equity, bonus or benefits

details.about: The Forecasting and Real-Time Optimization Platform (FORTOP) team sits in Lyft's Rideshare Experience & Marketplace org. It produces reliable, real-time supply and demand signals and forecasts that feed Lyft's automated marketplace decisions, including Dynamic Pricing, Real-Time Supply Management and Fulfillment. The work covers forecasting rider demand and driver supply as they shift with traffic, holidays and major events, and keeping systems correct and fast at peak times.
duties: Lead multi-engineer projects from proposal and technical design through launch, owning milestones, dependencies and estimates
Design and evolve streaming feature pipelines, training and inference workflows and signal serving; lead design reviews
Work with scientists to productionize ML models; build rollout tooling (shadow, canary, rollback) and backtesting and experimentation infrastructure
Own the interfaces, data contracts and SLAs between forecasting signals and consumers such as Dynamic Pricing and Driver Incentives
Monitor system health and signal quality, prepare for peak events, take part in on-call and lead post-incident work
Write well-tested code, give strong code reviews and coach teammates
Work with Product, Science and partner teams on problems, roadmap and trade-offs
Mentor engineers, help with hiring and onboarding, and share knowledge through docs and tech talks
needs: 5+ years of software engineering industry experience, including building and operating backend or data systems in production
BS/MS or equivalent in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, or relevant work experience
Experience designing and leading delivery of large-scale distributed systems and owning their reliability (monitoring, on-call, incident response)
Solid distributed-systems fundamentals: fault tolerance, delivery semantics and consistency trade-offs
A track record of leading ambiguous, multi-engineer projects and mentoring engineers
Clear written communication, including design docs
nice: Experience building production ML models and infrastructure
Hands-on stream or large-scale batch processing (Flink, Beam, Spark or similar) and messaging (Kafka, Kinesis or similar)
Time series forecasting systems, backtesting and forecast evaluation
Online experimentation or real-time decision systems such as pricing, dispatch or marketplace balancing
Comfort using AI-assisted development tools without compromising quality
details.benefits: Base pay $136,160 – $170,200 a year in the Seattle area, not including potential equity, bonus or benefits. Benefits include medical, dental and vision insurance, mental health benefits, family building benefits, child care and pet benefits, a 401(k) with company match, 12 observed holidays plus discretionary paid time off for salaried team members, 18 weeks of paid parental leave, subsidized commuter benefits, and monthly Lyft credits with a complimentary Lyft Pink membership.
notes: Hybrid: in the office Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays
Hybrid roles can work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks a year

yt_title: Lyft Is Hiring: Senior Software Engineer, Forecasting | Seattle, WA | $136K–$170K

scenes.head: Today's job
lines: Welcome to Veritas Recruitment Agency, where we bring you real tech jobs straight from employers' own careers sites.
Today, Lyft is hiring a Senior Software Engineer for forecasting and real-time optimization in Seattle, Washington, on a hybrid schedule.
You'll find the direct application link in the description.

scenes.head: About the team
lines: The team builds the Forecasting and Real-Time Optimization Platform, inside Lyft's rideshare marketplace group.
It turns streaming marketplace data into real-time supply and demand signals and forecasts, which power Dynamic Pricing, real-time supply management, and fulfillment.
That means predicting rider demand and driver supply as they shift with traffic, holidays, and big events.

scenes.head: What you'll do
bullets: Lead projects from design to launch
lines: You'll lead multi-engineer projects from technical design through launch.

You'll design streaming feature pipelines, model training and inference workflows, and the serving layer, and work with scientists to take models from prototype to production, with safe rollout tools like shadow, canary, and rollback.
You'll own the data contracts and service levels for teams like Dynamic Pricing, keep systems healthy at peak times, join the on-call rotation, and mentor other engineers.

scenes.head: What you need
bullets: BS/MS in CS or related, or equivalent
lines: You need five or more years of industry software engineering, including building and running backend or data systems in production, and a bachelor's or master's in computer science or a related field, or relevant work experience.
You should have led large-scale distributed systems and owned their reliability, with solid fundamentals like fault tolerance and consistency, plus clear design docs.
It's a plus if you've built production machine learning systems, used Flink, Spark, or Kafka, or worked on forecasting or real-time pricing and dispatch.

scenes.head: Pay & benefits
lines: The base pay range in the Seattle area is one hundred thirty-six thousand one hundred sixty to one hundred seventy thousand two hundred dollars a year, not including potential equity, bonus, or benefits.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision, mental health and family-building support, a four-oh-one-k with company match, eighteen weeks of paid parental leave, commuter benefits, and monthly Lyft credits.
The office days are Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and you can work from anywhere for up to four weeks a year.
